guide.title: How to update
guide.hint: Steps for this install method. Run them on the machine hosting the instance.

notes.install-sh: Re-run the installer's update helper from the folder it created.
notes.compose: Pull the new image and recreate the containers. Migrations run automatically on start.
notes.coolify: Open the resource in Coolify and press Redeploy (with “Pull latest images” enabled).
notes.dokploy: Open the application in Dokploy and press Deploy — it re-pulls the image.
notes.portainer: Open the stack in Portainer and press Update the stack with “Re-pull image” enabled.
notes.kubernetes: Point the deployment at the new image tag and wait for the rollout.
notes.dev: Pull the sources and reinstall dependencies, then restart the dev servers.
notes.unknown: The install method is unknown. Set MK_INSTALL_METHOD on the instance to get exact steps, or follow your deployment manager's redeploy action.

guide.backupWarning: Back up the database and uploads before updating — migrations are forward-only.

hook.title: One-click update
hook.hint: Paste the deploy webhook of your own deployment manager. “Update now” calls it so the manager pulls the new image and redeploys. Nothing is sent to us.
hook.detected: This instance looks like {method} — paste its deploy hook here.

source.title: Where do I get this hook?
source.hint: Pick your deployment manager — the hook lives in its own UI, you copy it once.
source.withoutToken: no bearer token — the URL itself authenticates

coolify.1: Open the resource you want redeployed in Coolify and copy its UUID — the last segment of the browser URL on the resource page.
coolify.2: Go to Keys & Tokens → API tokens and create a token with the “deploy” permission. Coolify shows it only once.
coolify.3: Paste that URL into “Deploy hook URL” with your Coolify host and that UUID, put the token in “Bearer token” and pick GET.

dokploy.1: Open the application (or Docker Compose service) in Dokploy and enable “Auto Deploy” on the General tab.
dokploy.2: Switch to the Deployments tab and copy the Webhook URL shown there.
dokploy.3: Paste it into “Deploy hook URL” and pick POST. The URL already carries its token, so leave “Bearer token” empty.

portainer.1: Open Stacks → your stack in Portainer and scroll to the Webhooks section.
portainer.2: Turn on “Create a stack webhook” and click Copy link. Enable “Re-pull image” under automatic updates so the redeploy actually fetches the new image (Business Edition).
portainer.3: Paste the link into “Deploy hook URL” and pick POST — no token is needed, the link itself is the secret.

other.1: Any HTTP endpoint that redeploys this instance works: a CI job trigger, an Argo CD sync webhook, a Watchtower HTTP trigger or a script of your own.
other.2: Paste its URL into “Deploy hook URL”, pick the HTTP method it expects and add a bearer token if it needs one. It is called exactly once per press, with no body.

disk.title: Disk usage
disk.subtitle: What the uploads directory on disk is made of, and the only cleanup that is safe without a retention policy.
disk.emptyHint: No uploaded file has landed in this instance, so the uploads directory is empty.

compositionHint.originals: The uploaded files themselves. Cannot be regenerated.
compositionHint.derivatives: Generated renditions. Can be rebuilt from the originals at any time.
compositionHint.unreferenced: On disk, claimed by no record — what a cleanup would take first.
compositionHint.unowned: Written by neither the attachment store nor a declared owner. Deletable by hand below.
compositionHint.reserved: Declared by a plugin as its own area. Managed by that plugin, never deleted here.

disk.missingFiles: {count} records point at a file that is no longer on disk. Their bytes are not counted above.

cleanup.keptHint: {count} more are younger than {hours}h and stay put.
cleanup.confirmMessage: {count} files ({size}) will be deleted. They are reachable by no attachment, project or chat, so nothing in the app can lose them.
cleanup.confirmKept: {count} more ({size}) are younger than {hours}h and will be kept — an upload still in flight looks the same from here.
cleanup.skipped: {count} files were left alone as too recent to judge
cleanup.failed: {count} files could not be deleted — see the server log
cleanup.error: Could not delete the unreferenced files
cleanup.none: Nothing to sweep — every stored file is either in use or too recent to judge.

reserved.title: Plugin areas
reserved.hint: Subtrees a plugin declared as its own — the phone-bridge keeps its downloaded tunnel client here, for instance. They count toward the total and are never deleted from this page.

browser.title: Browse files
browser.truncated: Only the first {count} entries are shown; drill into a directory to see the rest. Selecting all picks the visible rows.
browser.confirmMessage: {count} files ({size}) will be deleted. Files in use and plugin areas are kept regardless of the selection.
browser.confirmRecent: Anything written in the last {hours}h is kept too.
browser.kept: Kept: {claimed} in use, {reserved} plugin-owned, {recent} too recent
browser.failed: {count} files could not be deleted — see the server log
browser.deleteFailed: Could not delete the selected files
